newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to issue single bid document for Telebras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to issue single bid document for Telebras.

text.p: The Brazilian government will issue a single bid document for next year's privatization of the federal telecom system Telebras, Communications Minister Sergio Motta said.
"There will be one tender document, all of the companies together, with a closed envelope auction," Motta told reporters at a news conference.

At the conference, National Developpment Bank (BNDES) chief Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros said the government planned to extend cheap financing, already available to B Band cellular infrastructure investors, to fixed-line equipment makers.
Motta reiterated his plan to privatize the whole Telebras system by mid-1998.
The completed privatization would result in most of the ministry's functions being taken over by the sector watchdog ANTEL.
The minister said the selloff of Telebras, Latin America's largest telecommunications company, could be concluded in the first four to six months of 1998.

Motta also reiterated that the ministry would issue bid specifications for consultants to advise on the break-up and sale of Telebras on October 30. The winner would be announced 45 days later, he said.
The minister said the government would publish on August 29 tender details for bidding on cable television concessions.
Motta said there had been a lot of pressure to speed the privatization of cable services.
The ministry may publish specifications for two lots of 120 concessions each, he said.
Motta said tender details for satellite services were likely to be published on August 31. "It will be a closed envelope (auction) just like the B Band," he said.
The minister also said bid specifications for trunking services were likely to be published in September or October.
Trunking technology allows two-way radios to be used like cellular telephones.

Motta said the privatization of radio frequencies was "just about complete" and by the end of August or the middle of September the ministry should have sold off the first lot of 120 frequencies and be publishing the bid specfications for the second lot.
